successCriteria.description: The shared types module exports three string enums — LeaveType (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity), LeaveRequestStatus (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED), and UserRole (employee, manager, hr_admin) — each with exactly the specified values and no extras or missing members.

BaseRepository is an abstract class that cannot be instantiated directly and exposes six generic methods (query, findById, findAll, insert, update, delete) usable by concrete subclasses; a concrete subclass can be instantiated and all six methods are callable.
No `any` type appears anywhere in the shared types module, the base repository, or its unit tests — the no-any HARNESS constraint is satisfied (verified by typecheck and source search).

BaseRepository obtains its database connection exclusively from the shared pool exported by the db connection module; it does not instantiate its own Pool or import pg.Pool directly, satisfying the no-direct-db-outside-repository constraint at the foundation layer.

findById returns the matching row or null when absent; findAll returns an array (empty when the table has no rows); insert returns the inserted row; update returns the updated row or null when no row matches the id; delete returns a boolean indicating whether a row was removed (true when rowCount > 0, false otherwise).
Errors thrown by the underlying pool (connection failures, constraint violations, missing tables) propagate unchanged from every base repository method rather than being swallowed or masked.

The unit test suite for the base repository covers, at minimum: successful query/find/insert/update/delete, not-found (null) for findById and update, empty-array for findAll, error propagation from the pool, constraint-violation error propagation on insert, and the true/false boolean return of delete — all without using `any`.
The project builds cleanly (tsc --noEmit exits 0) and the Jest unit tests pass (jest --passWithNoTests exits 0) with the shared types and base repository in place.

constraints: No `any` types anywhere in the shared types module, base repository, or its tests — use `unknown` with type guards / `Record<string, unknown>` instead (HARNESS no-any, severity high).

All database access in the base repository must go through the shared `pool` exported by the db connection module; the base class must not instantiate its own Pool or bypass the repository pattern (HARNESS no-direct-db-outside-repository, severity critical; GP-001).
TypeScript strict mode must pass — no implicit any, strict null checks — per tsconfig.json (strict: true) and AGENTS.md.
The base repository must use TypeScript generics on its data-access methods so concrete repositories can obtain typed rows without casts to `any`.

The base repository must NOT accept a `client: PoolClient` parameter or implement transaction joining in Phase 1 — transaction support is deferred to concrete repositories in later phases per the reconciled architecture's Transaction Contract.
No hardcoded secrets, passwords, API keys, or tokens in the shared types or base repository (HARNESS no-hardcoded-secrets, severity critical).
No `@gestalt/*` packages may be added as project dependencies (HARNESS no-gestalt-internal-deps, severity critical).
outOfScope: Employee model, repository, and service (Phase 2) — not created in this phase despite the reconciled architecture grouping "Shared types + Employee foundation" together; PLAN.md Phase 1 is limited to shared types and the base repository only.
Concrete domain repositories (Employee, LeavePolicy, LeaveBalance, LeaveRequest, AuditLog, Notification) — Phases 2–7; the base repository is abstract and provides only generic helpers.

Transaction joining via an optional `client: PoolClient` parameter — deferred to concrete repository methods in Phases 2–7 per the Transaction Contract; the base class query helper does not accept a client.
Service layers, controllers, Fastify routes, RBAC guards, and audit/notification wiring — Phases 8–10.
Database migrations / Knex schema definitions for the conceptual tables — not part of this phase; the base repository operates on table names passed by callers.
Error type classes in src/shared/error-types.ts — referenced by ARCHITECTURE.md module structure but not in PLAN.md Phase 1 scope; the base repository propagates raw pool errors.

entityInvariants.invariant: The enum is closed over exactly six members — annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity — each mapping to its lowercase string value; no member may be added, removed, or renamed without a reconciled-architecture change, because every LeavePolicy and LeaveBalance in later phases keys off these values.

The enum is closed over exactly five members — DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED — each mapping to its uppercase string value; these are the only valid lifecycle states a LeaveRequest may hold, and the LeaveRequest state machine in Phase 9 depends on this exact set.

The enum is closed over exactly three members — employee, manager, hr_admin — each mapping to its lowercase string value; these are the only roles the Auth Contract (request.user.role) and RBAC guards in Phase 10 may accept.

BaseRepository is abstract and cannot be instantiated directly; it provides only generic, table-parameterized query helpers and owns no domain-specific logic, so every concrete repository in Phases 2–7 must extend it rather than re-implementing pool access.

interfaceConstraints.operation: BaseRepository.query — execute an arbitrary parameterized SQL text against the shared pool and return the typed QueryResult
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Any error from the underlying pool (connection, syntax, constraint) must propagate to the caller unchanged; the method must not swallow or transform it.

interfaceConstraints.operation: BaseRepository.findById — select a single row by primary key from a named table
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the row when found, null when no row matches; pool errors propagate unchanged.

interfaceConstraints.operation: BaseRepository.findAll — select all rows from a named table
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns an array of rows (empty array when the table has no rows); pool errors propagate unchanged.

interfaceConstraints.operation: BaseRepository.insert — insert a row from a key/value map into a named table and return the inserted row
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the inserted row (via RETURNING *); constraint-violation and other pool errors propagate unchanged.

interfaceConstraints.operation: BaseRepository.update — update the row matching a primary key in a named table from a key/value map and return the updated row
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the updated row when a row matched (via RETURNING *), null when no row matched the id; pool errors propagate unchanged.

interfaceConstraints.operation: BaseRepository.delete — delete the row matching a primary key from a named table
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns true when a row was removed (rowCount > 0), false when no row matched; pool errors propagate unchanged.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The base repository must import and use the single shared `pool` exported from the db connection module (new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL, ... })) rather than creating its own Pool, so that all repositories share one connection pool and the no-direct-db-outside-repository constraint holds at the foundation.

The three exported enums (LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, UserRole) must match exactly the value sets declared in the reconciled architecture's domain_entities and modules sections — LeaveType: annual|sick|emergency|unpaid|maternity|paternity; LeaveRequestStatus: DRAFT|SUBMITTED|APPROVED|REJECTED|CANCELLED; UserRole: employee|manager|hr_admin — because every downstream module (employee, leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-request, audit, notification) imports from shared-types per the dependency map.
All shared types and base repository source must compile under the project's strict CommonJS/ES2022 tsconfig (strict: true, baseUrl: ./src) so that `npm run build` (tsc --noEmit) exits 0.

The base repository unit tests must run under the project's ts-jest configuration (preset: ts-jest, testMatch: **/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js), moduleDirectories including src) so that `npx jest --passWithNoTests` discovers and passes them.

The base repository must remain a thin, generic, table-parameterized helper with no domain-specific query logic, consistent with ARCHITECTURE.md's "thin repository layer" pattern and the module boundary that places shared utilities (db connection, base repository, error types) under src/shared/.

integrationPoints.target: src/shared/types/index.ts → all domain modules (employee, leave-policy, leave-balance, leave-request, audit, notification) in Phases 2–7
integrationPoints.why: Every concrete repository and service imports LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, and/or UserRole from this module per the reconciled dependency map (all modules → shared-types); the enum value sets are the contract those modules compile against.

integrationPoints.target: src/shared/base-repository.ts → concrete Pg*Repository classes (PgEmployeeRepository, PgLeavePolicyRepository, PgLeaveBalanceRepository, PgLeaveRequestRepository, PgAuditLogRepository, PgNotificationRepository) in Phases 2–7
integrationPoints.why: Each concrete repository extends BaseRepository to inherit the generic query/find/insert/update/delete helpers and shared pool access, satisfying GP-001 (repository pattern) and the no-direct-db-outside-repository constraint without re-implementing pool wiring.

integrationPoints.target: src/shared/db/connection.ts → src/shared/base-repository.ts (and transitively all concrete repositories)
integrationPoints.why: The single shared pool is the only database connection source; the base repository consumes it and every concrete repository inherits that consumption, ensuring one connection pool across the application.
